transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I'm here because I just keep blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. I've been snapping on my operations calls at work, and I'm even doing it at home with my family. That is just not how I've ever handled things before, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized or keyed up?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel energized. If anything, I'm just constantly on edge and irritated, but I don't have this extra energy or feel keyed up in that way. I'm just snapping at everyone.
Did this start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

Yeah, it did. Um... this has all been going on for about three weeks now. It started right after we had a valve failure at the facility, and... well, there was an injury when it happened. Ever since then, I've just been like this.
Since this started, have you been feeling down or depressed?

No, I wouldn't say I feel depressed. I'm not... sad or down in the dumps or anything like that. It's really just the anger and the constant feeling like I'm on edge. I don't feel like crying or staying in bed, I just can't seem to stop snapping at people.
Do memories of the valve failure or the injury keep popping into your mind when you don’t want them to?

Yeah, they really do. I can just be sitting at the kitchen table, or trying to answer some emails from home, and suddenly I’m right back there. I see the flash from that valve and the smoke in the aisle. It just... it happens out of nowhere, like it completely shoves everything else out of my head.
Have you been avoiding reminders of the valve failure?

No, not really. I mean, I still have to work, so I can't completely avoid the facility or anything. I don't go out of my way to hide from it or pretend it didn't happen. It's just... there. I still talk to the guys at work about what needs to be fixed. I'm not avoiding it, it's just always in the back of my mind.
When those memories hit, do you ever feel like you’re actually back at the valve failure, as if it’s happening again?

No, I wouldn't say I feel like I'm actually back there. It's more like... I just see it really clearly in my head. I know I'm still sitting in my kitchen or wherever I am, but the image of it is just so strong. It's not like I lose touch with reality or think the explosion is happening right then and there. It's just a really intense memory that I can't shake.
Since the valve failure, have you been feeling unusually jumpy or easily startled?

Yeah, definitely. It's like I'm constantly on edge now. Any time I hear a forklift beep at work, or a compressor kick on... even if the smoke alarm just chirps at home because the battery is low, my whole body just tightens up. I immediately start looking around for the exits and trying to figure out what's going to go wrong next. I just can't seem to relax.
Have these symptoms been interfering with your ability to do your job or handle things at home?

Yeah, it's... it's definitely messing things up. I actually haven't even been cleared to go back to the plant yet. I'm trying to work from home, but honestly, I'm missing things on calls. I'm just not focusing. I've ended up upsetting a few people because I'm dropping the ball. I'm honestly starting to worry that I'm becoming a liability to the company instead of the manager they need me to be.
